figure_annotations.summary:
a	The chart illustrates a timeline of a single ALE cycle showing the values of the following process parameters: DC power, ICP power, CF4+H2 flow rate, and Ar flow rate .
b	The figure illustrate a schematic overview of the dosing of reactants on a surface based on the timedependent information shown in subfigure a.
figure_annotations.q1: What are the three main steps of this ALE cycle and what function fullfills the last sub-cycle?
figure_annotations.a1: The three main parts in this ALE cycle are the dosing of a plasma containing Ar, CH4, and H2 related species, a plasma exposure, solely consisting of Ar, and lastly a Ar plasma exposure with a biased substrate. This last step is introduced to enable energetic ions to bombard the substrate, leading to selective etching.
figure_annotations.q2: Based on the figure, is it likely that due to the ALE process the final substrate will contain carbon and fluorine contaminations, and what could be the reason of this?
figure_annotations.a2: Yes, in the most right part of subfigure b, there are still CF groups present at the surface. This incomplete removal by the Ar ions can be related to the ion energy as well as the binding energy of these groups to the surface.
figure_annotations.q3: Is the pressure in the reactor chamber constant during this process?
figure_annotations.q4: What information is missing in subfigure a, that prevents the reproduction of this process?
figure_annotations.a4: To be able to reproduce this experiment the dosing times should be present.

figure_annotations.summary:
a	The figure shows the deposition rate on various materials (Si, Al2O3, HfO2, AlN, TiN, SiO2) against the percentage of CF4 in the process.
b	The figure illustrates the concentration of F, CF2, and CF radical species against the percentage of CF4 in the process.
figure_annotations.q1: Which materials are etched upon exposure to a plasma with more than 10% CF4 added to the plasma?
figure_annotations.a1: The materials are TiN and SiO2
figure_annotations.q2: Which material should be used as substrate to have the highest film deposition rate?
figure_annotations.a2: The material that should be used as substrate is AlNx
figure_annotations.q3: Which radical concentration has the highest dependence on CF4 concentration?
figure_annotations.a3: The radical concentration of CF has the highest dependence on the CF4 concentration.
figure_annotations.q4: By adding more CF4 to the plasma composition can different starting substrates be identified?
figure_annotations.a4: An experiment can be designed such that initial thickness and final thickness can be determined after exposure to the plasma. Some materials thicknesses will decrease, others will increase.

figure_annotations.q1: How is the fluorine content related to the CF4 concentration in the used plasma?
figure_annotations.a1: Based on subfigure a, it is shown that an increase in the CF4 concentration results in more fluorine in the film.
figure_annotations.q2: How does the CF4 concentration determine the stoichiometry of the film?
figure_annotations.a2: An increase in CF4 concentration seems to induce a shift from more CF3 and C-CFx bonds towards more CF and CF2 bonds.
figure_annotations.q3: Can the shift in peak position for fluorine say something about the stoichiometry?
figure_annotations.a3: Yes, usually a shift in peak position indicates different stoichiometries. This is proven by the spectrum from carbon where the change in stoichiometry also introduces different peaks.
figure_annotations.q4: can it be said that there is more carbon in the film in the case that the CF4 concentration is 3.3% with respect to the 6.6% case?
figure_annotations.a4: This conclusion can not be drawn from the bare carbon spectrum. Calculations of atomic composition require more material specific parameters than the pure XPS spectrum.

figure_annotations.figure_caption: Fig. 4. The etch rate over modification step duration a) for all studied materials, and b) enlarged for  $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ ,  $\mathrm{AlN_x}$ , and  $\mathrm{HfO_2}$ .
figure_annotations.class:
a	multiple line chart
b	multiple line chart
figure_annotations.summary:
a	The etch rate increases linearly for SiO2 and reaches an optimum for the other materials with the modification step duration, the only material that does not etch is TiN.
b	The etch rate initially increases, peaks at around 10 seconds, and then decreases for all materials.
figure_annotations.q1: a	Can SiO2 be partially selective be etch with respect to any of the other materials, and if so, for which conditions?
figure_annotations.a1: a	SiO2 has a way higher etch rate than for example HfO2, at 15 s of modification duration. This indicates that SiO2, at least partially, can selectively be etch with respect to HfO2.
figure_annotations.q2: a	Which material has the highest etch resistance for these chemistries?
figure_annotations.a2: a	TiN does not etch for any modification duration.
figure_annotations.q3: b	What modification time is most likely used for industrial applications when etching AlNx?
figure_annotations.a3: b	5 s of modification duration is most likely used as this would have similar etch results as longer times, but reduces the processing time.
figure_annotations.q4: b	Is there only etching upon a modification step, and how can you tell?
figure_annotations.a4: b	No there is continuous etching. For all three materials the etch rate is non-zero at 0 s modification duration.

figure_annotations.summary: a	The chart shows the etch rate of various materials (Al2O3, HfO2, AlNx, TiN, SiO2) against the activation step duration. The etch rate increases with time for all materials.
figure_annotations.q1: For the etching of aluminum based material, does it matter which type of material it is (i.e. nitride/oxide)?
figure_annotations.a1: No it does not seem to matter. Both Al2O3 and AlNx have similar etch results.
figure_annotations.q2: Based on these results is it possible to have selective ALE, if so, which material can be selectively etched?
figure_annotations.a2: Yes it is possible, SiO2 can be selectively etched wrt to all other materials at an activation time of 5 seconds.
figure_annotations.q3: Based on this data, can an ALE recipe be developed for TiN?
figure_annotations.a3: Yes, there is an increase in etch rate for increasing activation time
figure_annotations.q4: Which activation step durations should be applied to have similar etching of HfO2 and Al2O3?
figure_annotations.a4: 20 s for HfO2 and 10 s for Al2O3.

figure_annotations.figure_caption: Fig. 6. The etch depth over the number of cycles in ALE process (activation step duration is  $10~\mathrm{s}$ ).
figure_annotations.q1: For which material are more datapoints required to have a more reliable linear fit and what implications are there if this is not done?
figure_annotations.a1: SiO2 does not show that good of a fit. This suggests that, if the characterization is performed well, that the process is not that controlled. This in turn suggests that perfect ALE is not acquired.
figure_annotations.q2: From the materials that actually etch, which one has the highest etch resistivity?
figure_annotations.a2: HfO2 shows the highest etch resistivity as for this material, the total etch depth is the lowest.
figure_annotations.q3: What two materials can be used together, for which no two ALE processes have to be used to get similar results?
figure_annotations.q4: How many cycles are required to reach an etch depth of 20 nm for SiO2?

figure_annotations.figure_caption: Fig. 7. The  $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$  etch (nm/cycle) rate distribution across the wafer. The ordinate axis is the radius from the center of the wafer. The numbers around are the polar angle.
figure_annotations.summary: a	The polar chart displays the relationship between the location on the wafer and etch rate of Al2O3.
figure_annotations.q1: What is the highest observed difference in etch rate on the wafer?
figure_annotations.a1: The largest difference in etch rate is 0.008 nm/cycle
figure_annotations.q2: What can be a reason for non-uniformity in processing?
figure_annotations.a2: An explanation for non-uniformity in ALE processes is the non-uniform distribution of reactants in the reactor.
figure_annotations.q3: Which trend can be identified regarding the dependence of the etch rate on the position in the reactor?
figure_annotations.a3: There seems to be solely a radial dependence. There is no uni-directional trend visible.
figure_annotations.q4: Where has the etch process the highest performance (i.e. etch rate)?
figure_annotations.a4: In the center of the reactor, in a circle with a radius of around 1 cm.
